history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2462 ('Mahishmardini Temple, Bakreshwar', Bakreshwar, West Bengal) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 1193 / id bakreshwar-temple-birbhum, which already documents the Bakreshwar Shakti Peetha complex including the Mahishmardini principal shrine. Multiple consulted sources explicitly describe the complex as containing the Mahishmardini shrine (with ancient goddess paintings preserved by the ASI, principal black-stone idol in the garbhagriha) alongside the Vakranath temple; no separate independent 'Mahishmardini Temple' distinct from the Shakti Peetha complex was found. It is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas: the centre of Sati's eyebrows (symbolic of her mind) is believed to have fallen here. A separate file is written per the schema; consider MERGING or dropping in favour of seq 1193. Coordinates identical to seq 1193 (same complex).

name: Mahishmardini Temple, Bakreshwar
town_description: Bakreshwar is a pilgrim village on the southern bank of the Bakreshwar (Paphara) stream in Birbhum district, ~7 miles north-west of Dubrajpur and ~18 km south-west of Suri — called the 'village of deities' for its many temples, also noted for its thermal springs and the nearby Bakreshwar Thermal Power Station township.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata (~230 km); Kazi Nazrul Islam Airport Durgapur ~51 km (verify)
travel.railway: Dubrajpur (~7 miles / ~11.7 km); Sainthia Junction also cited
travel.road: Metalled road Suri-Dubrajpur via Bakreshwar; direct buses from Suri, Dubrajpur, Bolpur, Sainthia and Durgapur

visitor_information.best_time: October-March (winter is ideal for hot-spring bathing); Navratri is the grandest period but crowded
